findings.location: Question keys size-alone, magnification, rods-versus-linear, amorphous-distribution, no-correlate, round-group-followup, stable-suspicious, modifiers-not-score, mri-4a-selected, mri-4b-risk; DE/EN/FA
findings.evidence: Many alternatives are unrelated or absolute: magnification competes with measuring breast density or detecting enhancement; rods-versus-linear with visible only on MRI; size-alone with smaller means certainly malignant; mri-4a-selected with a negative MRI upgrading to category5. The correct options repeatedly carry the longest integrated qualification. These patterns occur throughout both producer modules.
findings.learnerImpact: Learners can score well through test-taking cues without distinguishing plausible diagnostic or management errors. Complete feedback does not repair low discrimination.
findings.requiredCorrection: Rewrite the full18-item pool around meaningful diagnostic decisions, balancing option specificity and length. Use plausible competing descriptors, genuinely confusable distributions, work-up adequacy, temporal comparison, and realistic management errors. Retain stable IDs; do not impose a question quota. Independently reread every alternative and all162 localized wrong-answer explanations.
findings.retestEvidence: Not repaired or retested in this baseline review.

findings.location: mammaCalcificationReview.js cards mammographie-mikrokalk-mri4a and -mri4b5; questions mri-4a-selected/mri-4b-risk; page.js TakeHomeList last item
findings.evidence: The lesson correctly says confirmed mammographic category4/5 retains a biopsy indication, and question4A explicitly says biopsy is standard. Card4B instead leads with individual decision/usually biopsy. The4A card says studies discuss6–12 months without identifying this as a discussion proposal rather than a validated surveillance protocol. The closing takeaway mentions selected MRI-supported biopsy avoidance without restating the research boundary.
findings.learnerImpact: Flashcard retrieval can teach category4B surveillance as a routine alternative and make a research interval look like established management, despite the more careful lesson table.
findings.requiredCorrection: State category4 tissue diagnosis consistently first in lesson, questions and cards. Preserve the fact that selected MRI research explores avoidance, but explicitly identify the proposed/modelled nature, study selection and limitations. Do not derive residual risk from category alone or present22% as an established category4A/4B treatment boundary. Source6–12 months to Fueger discussion and make clear it was not prospectively validated as an omission schedule.
findings.retestEvidence: Not repaired or retested in this baseline review.

findings.location: mammaMammographyCalcifications.js card mammographie-mikrokalk-06; content.js MORPH risk labels
findings.evidence: Card06 teaches an unqualified ordered arrow amorphous → coarse heterogeneous → fine pleomorphic → fine linear/branching. Linked taxonomy reinforces low–moderate versus moderate for the first pair. Primary cohorts do not support a universal strict first-pair ordering: Bent2010 reports equal risks; Youk2019 reports a reversed derivation ordering and no significant first-pair difference.
findings.learnerImpact: Learners may substitute a memorized linear ranking for morphology plus distribution and context.
findings.requiredCorrection: Teach all suspicious descriptors without a deterministic amorphous-versus-coarse ranking. Explain context/cohort dependence, retain the higher concern of fine linear/branching patterns, and preserve the distinction between coarse benign and coarse heterogeneous.
findings.retestEvidence: Not repaired or retested in this baseline review.

findings.location: page.js CALC_MATRIX, MORPH round input and KalkAssessment; content.js MORPH
findings.evidence: All25 cells reproduce the historical Youk coefficient/cutoff model, rather than an ACR automatic morphology×distribution table. Existing caption explicitly calls it a study model and category3 output has a clinical-check warning; these safeguards are acknowledged. Missing at the decision point are selected excision-cohort limits and the original predictor scope: Youk used punctate, whereas the input is generalized to round. Prominent result still combines a BI-RADS number, standard risk range and action.
findings.learnerImpact: The interface can overgeneralize a historical research result to every round calcification and make cohort-model output feel like a clinical classification.
findings.requiredCorrection: Keep historical model and current clinical assessment visibly distinct. Identify the limited original punctate predictor, selected population, and absent temporal/patient inputs. Use an explicit worked example showing why model3 cannot prescribe surveillance and why model-derived categories do not replace clinical assessment. A different presentation is acceptable; no automatic cell recategorization is requested.
findings.retestEvidence: Not repaired or retested in this baseline review.

findings.location: page.js Ausdehnung RememberNote: unabhängig von der Morphologie ein eigenständiger Risikofaktor
findings.evidence: The lesson correctly labels its extent percentages as a biopsy-cohort PPV. It then asserts morphology-independent risk. The cited Metaxa2019 observational comparison supports an association of increasing extent with malignancy; the accessed primary text does not establish this statement by a reported morphology-adjusted analysis.
findings.learnerImpact: A cohort association is taught as an independent predictive effect, encouraging causal or patient-specific interpretation of the chart.
findings.requiredCorrection: Either narrow the wording to the demonstrated cohort association or cite and explain an appropriate adjusted primary analysis. Preserve the distinction between total extent, particle size and treatment-planning relevance. Verify chart values and bins directly against the original table before acceptance.
